plates.title: The Funnel and the Loop
plates.prompt: An illuminated manuscript page, tall format, cream vellum ground, thin gold-leaf rule-lines dividing the page into four horizontal bands from top to bottom, each band a cluster of small framed ink-and-muted-pigment scenes in strict reading order, connected by fine red hairline paths with small arrowheads. TOP BAND (three scenes left to right): THE RHINOCEROS HORN — an apothecary holding a curved horn to a customer while a scribe crosses the remedy off a list; THE KEY UNDER WATER — a man rubbing a key over running water in a crowded bathroom, the key unbent; THE COCKTAIL PARTY TEST — two guests chatting easily while an unconcerned hostess looks on. A path leads down into the SECOND BAND (three scenes): THE BAMBOO CONTROLLER — an islander in a reed hut wearing wooden headphone-shapes and bamboo antennas, staring at an empty runway with unlit fires; LEANING OVER BACKWARDS — a robed scholar bent backward over his own open ledger, pen still raised; a short path branching to MILLIKAN'S FALLING DROP in the THIRD BAND — a scientist watching an oil drop fall between brass plates, recording a figure. The THIRD BAND continues with THE EASIEST PERSON TO FOOL — the same scholar holding a round mirror to his own doubting face; and THE LOW-NICOTINE CIGARETTE — a merchant holding up a cigarette packet while a second packet hides in shadow behind his back. A path descends to the FOURTH BAND: THE CORRIDOR OF SAND — a researcher pouring sand along a long corridor of identical doors as a rat pauses on the new floor; THE SHRINKING EFFECT — a line of robed figures each holding a fainter glowing card, the last an empty palm. At the bottom, alone, FREEDOM TO KEEP FAITH — a scholar standing at an open hilltop gate at dusk, looking back down the road. From this final scene, a long thin gold ribbon-path curves up the right margin of the page and loops back to re-enter the top band beside THE RHINOCEROS HORN, closing the circuit. Palette: faded ochre, iron-gall brown ink, muted blue and dull red pigment, gold leaf only on the rule-lines and the looping ribbon. Each scene sits in its own thin rectangular ink frame with generous interior space so the figures read clearly; modest foliate scrollwork fills gaps between frames but never crowds them. Each vignette has its capitalized title lettered directly beneath its frame in a plain manuscript hand; nothing else on the page is lettered — no headings, no banners, no scrolls bearing writing, no signature.

plates.title: The Survey of What Fails
plates.prompt: An illuminated manuscript page, tall format, cream vellum ground, a single continuous winding path in faded red ink running top to bottom and linking eight framed scenes in order, like a pilgrim's road through a survey of false cures. First scene, top: THE RHINOCEROS HORN — an apothecary offers a curved horn across a counter while a scholar crosses it from a list of trials. The path descends to A CONVERSATION ABOUT UFO'S — a man gestures at a glowing disc in the sky to seated listeners surrounded by charts. Next, FLOATING IN THE TANK — a man floats eyes-closed in a dark salted-water tank, lid ajar. The path forks briefly to two neighboring scenes sharing one frame-width: THE DENT IN THE TOE — a man presses a woman's bare toe on a massage table while a skeptical bather watches; and BETTER UNDER WATER — a small crowd huddles at a running sink, one holding a key beneath the water while another rubs it. The path rejoins and continues to THE SINKING SCORES — a teacher holds a chart whose line of marks dips lower each year before empty desks. Then THE COCKTAIL PARTY TEST — two guests converse easily over glasses while an unconcerned hostess passes. Last scene, bottom: UNTESTED REMEDIES — a patient reclines on a couch before a robed figure and a shelf of identical unlabeled jars, a long pinned list of remedies behind them. Palette throughout: faded ochre vellum, iron-gall brown line work, muted dull blue and red pigment, a little gold leaf only on the connecting path and the thin rectangular frames around each scene. Leave generous space inside each frame so every figure and gesture is clearly visible; modest foliate scrollwork may fill the narrow gaps between frames but must never crowd the scenes themselves, and the scenes should use the full width of the page rather than huddling in a central column. Each vignette carries its capitalized title lettered plainly beneath its frame in a manuscript hand. Nothing else on the page is lettered — no headings, no banners, no scrolls or ledgers bearing writing, no signature, no date.

plates.title: The Four Checks Skipped
plates.prompt: An illuminated manuscript page, tall format, cream vellum ground, a single continuous winding path in faded red ink running top to bottom through eight framed scenes, like a corridor the reader walks down. First, top: THE RAT'S OLD DOOR — a researcher sketches a maze at a desk beside a small rat and a chalk-marked door. The path leads to REPEATING THE FIRST RUN — the same figure builds a matching maze beside the first and places an identical rat at its start. Next, THE PROFESSOR'S REFUSAL — an older robed professor holds up a flat hand, turning the young researcher away from her second maze. The path continues to THE MISSING COMPARISON — a technician beside a vast ringed machine directs a beam into one labeled vessel of heavy hydrogen while a second vessel for light hydrogen sits empty and unused nearby. Then THE CORRIDOR OF DOORS — a long wooden corridor lined with identical doors on each side, a rat running straight down its middle toward one marked door. Next, THE SOUND OF THE FLOOR — the researcher kneels with ear to the floorboards as the rat's feet strike the wood, small sound-lines drawn radiating from its paws. Then GONE THE SECOND TIME — a robed researcher holds a glowing card bright before a seated subject in one frame, and the same card faded to blankness in the neighboring frame. Last, bottom: ONLY THE ONES WHO SCORE — a teacher at a lectern waves away a row of hopeful students with empty hands, beckoning forward only the one holding a glowing card. Palette: faded ochre vellum, iron-gall brown ink line work, muted dull blue and red pigment, gold leaf only on the connecting path and the thin rectangular frames. Give each scene generous interior space so every figure, door, and gesture reads clearly across the width of the page, not crowded into a narrow column; modest foliate scrollwork may fill the gaps between frames but must never crowd the scenes. Each vignette carries its capitalized title lettered plainly beneath its frame in a manuscript hand. Nothing else on the page is lettered — no headings, no banners, no scrolls or ledgers bearing writing, no signature, no date.
